rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: rethink the semester load with a leave option [Revision]
rows.description: When the illness lasts longer, the student meets an adviser and reduces the course load or takes a term break, with a plan to return. Adapting the goal is better than failing several courses.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: avoid telling the college and hide poor results [Pitfall]
rows.description: Fearing judgement, the student says nothing and misses classes without explanation. Grades fall and the department, unaware, applies standard penalties.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
rows.subtype: Approach: learn from hospital staff how to help at home [Action]
rows.description: The student asks nurses to show basic care such as safe lifting and diet instructions, and writes them down. Learning from professionals makes home care safer and less stressful.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, commitment device, contingency planning, prioritising, time-boxing

rows.subtype: Approach: implementation intention with a fixed cue [Thinking]
rows.description: The young professional decides: after I brush my teeth in the morning, I walk for 20 minutes. Linking the habit to an existing routine removes the daily decision.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, contingency planning, copying without fit, pre-mortem, rigid persistence, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: start with a tiny version that can be done on bad days [Action]
rows.description: The person begins with ten minutes of stretching and a short jog rather than a one-hour gym session, and adds time each week. Small steps build consistency before intensity.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, contingency planning, copying without fit, if-then plan, pre-mortem, rigid persistence

rows.subtype: Approach: all-or-nothing plan with a five-day-a-week gym [Pitfall]
rows.description: Motivated on 1 January, the person signs up for a year and plans daily hard workouts. A cold and a busy week break the streak, and the person drops the whole plan feeling like a failure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, contingency planning, copying without fit, if-then plan, pre-mortem, rigid persistence

rows.subtype: Approach: accountability with a friend and a shared log [Action]
rows.description: Two colleagues agree to message each other after each session and to meet at the park twice a week. A partner makes skipping costlier and workouts more pleasant.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: contingency planning, copying without fit, if-then plan, pre-mortem, rigid persistence, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: copy an influencer's routine and diet [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person follows a reel plan of extreme calorie cuts and heavy lifts without regard to the body or schedule. Soreness and hunger cause quitting within two weeks, since borrowed routines may not fit.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, contingency planning, if-then plan, pre-mortem, rigid persistence, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: pre-mortem on why the habit may fail [Thinking]
rows.description: The person imagines quitting in a month and lists likely causes: late meetings, monsoon, tiredness. Each gets a plan, such as home workouts or a shift to morning.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, contingency planning, copying without fit, if-then plan, rigid persistence, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: track and adjust after a missed week [Revision]
rows.description: After missing a week, the person does not scrap the plan but notes that late evenings fail and moves sessions to mornings, with a rule of never missing twice in a row. Treating a lapse as data keeps the habit alive.
